self.title: Revision: Cognitive Foundations of Personal Identity

detail.title: Revision: Cognitive Foundations of Personal Identity
detail.summary: Personal identity is sustained through the recursive process of autobiographical memory and narrative integration. Evidence confirms that identity is not a static archive but a reconstructive process, where the 'self' is shaped by the framing of past experiences.
detail.reason: Revising established findings with new source integration regarding narrative construction.

detail.title: Cognitive Foundations of Personal Identity
detail.question: How do memory continuity and narrative integration contribute to the persistence of personal identity?
detail.reason: Attention is currently focused on the 'identity' domain; this project addresses the core question of continuity and self-concept within that constraint.

children.title: Cycle 10 · Journal of Identity and Observer Epistemology

detail.title: Journal of Identity and Observer Epistemology
detail.summary: This cycle progresses the research on personal identity construction and observer epistemology. Notebooks for 'Cognitive Foundations of Personal Identity' and 'Epistemological Foundations of Observer Disagreement' have been synthesized using the collected sources, documenting the reconstructive nature of memory and the role of framing in disagreement. A follow-up research action on curious exploration mechanisms is initiated.
